message:
Wait, I need to reconsider the trace. The fix commit shows that the vulnerable code is:

```c
if ((caps = memchr(line, '\0', len)) != NULL) {
    caps++;
    if (strncmp(caps, "object-format=", CONST_STRLEN("object-format=")) == 0)
```

The fix adds the check `len > (size_t)((caps - line) + 1)`. So the vulnerability is that when the null byte is at the very end of the packet data (position `len - 1` from `line`), `caps++` points one past the packet data. But since the buffer is zeroed, `caps` would point to `buf->data + 65535` (the last byte of the buffer), not past it.

Wait, let me reconsider. The packet data is 65531 bytes. The `line` is `buf->data + 4`. The packet data occupies `buf->data + 4` to `buf->data + 4 + 65531 - 1 = buf->data + 65534`.

If the null byte is at position 65530 (0-indexed from `line`), that's at `buf->data + 4 + 65530 = buf->data + 65534`. Then `caps = line + 65530 + 1 = buf->data + 4 + 65531 = buf->data + 65535`. Then `caps++` makes `caps = buf->data + 65536`, which is one past the end of the buffer.

So `strncmp(caps, "object-format=", 14)` reads from `buf->data + 65536`, which is past the end of the buffer. That's the heap-buffer-overflow.

But wait, I need to verify that `buf->data + 65536` is actually past the end of the heap allocation. The `buffer_data` is the last member of `transport_smart`. Let me check:

<｜｜DSML｜｜>
<parameter=command>grep -n "buffer_data" /workspace/repo-vul/src-vul/libgit2/src/libgit2/transports/smart.h</｜｜DSML｜｜>
</｜｜DSML｜｜>
